RFC7311-3-1.note: Judge 2026-09-30. TestRFC7311AIGPTLVLengthIsEleven: + WriteTo emits 01 000b and 8 value octets and ParseAIGP reads the metric back; - Type-1 TLVs of Length 12 and 10 are refused by ParseAIGP, the registered parser. Forbidden: accepting a Type-1 TLV whose Length is not 11. Records observed red (AIGPMetricOffset).

RFC7311-3-2.note: Judge 2026-09-30. TestRFC7311AIGPValueIsWholeTLVSet: + a value of two whole TLVs parses into exactly those two; - one, two or three trailing octets that do not form a TLV are refused. Forbidden: accepting a value that is not a whole set of TLVs.

RFC7311-3-3.note: RFC 7311 Section 3: 'Any other AIGP TLVs in the AIGP attribute MUST be passed along unchanged if the AIGP attribute is passed along.' Re-read all four tagged units. TestRFC7311OtherAIGPTLVsPassedAlongUnchanged compares the complete trailing second Type-1 and unknown Type-9 TLVs byte-for-byte at the final socket for unchanged next hop and next-hop-self, despite a policy replacement that drops them; it separately asserts first metric 100/130. TestRFC7311OtherAIGPTLVsSurviveTheCodec supplies conforming complete-byte roundtrip and first-TLV selection, supplemented by TestParseAIGPMultipleTLVs and TestAIGPWriteToMultipleTLVs. Valid lengths isolate preservation, not malformed-input rejection. Producers attribute.ParseAIGP/AIGP.WriteTo and reactor.applyFactsAIGP preserve all received bytes and modify only the first metric; fwdBatchHandler reaches Session.writeUpdateBody with AIGP enabled. Dropping, rewriting or accumulating the second metric would fail the exact assertions. The ownership fixture establishes admissible forwarded identity, not the RFC verdict; the socket octets establish the conditional whole obligation. Producer-halt records alone were not used as semantic proof.

RFC7311-3.2-4.note: Forbidden: keeping or passing along an AIGP whose transitive bit is set. TestRFC7606AIGPTransitiveIsDiscarded asserts Action==AttributeDiscard on code 26 with DiscardReasonMalformedValue and require.False(found) for AIGP after ApplyAttrDiscard, with ORIGIN, AS_PATH, NEXT_HOP intact; TestRFC7311AIGPTransitiveDiscardedOnReceive asserts the same through enforceRFC7606 with no error (discard, not reset). Positives with flags 0x80 assert RFC7606ActionNone and the AIGP bytes unchanged, so a codepoint-only check goes red.

RFC7311-3.2-5.note: Forbidden: acting on, or passing along, a malformed AIGP, or escalating beyond ignoring it. TestAIGPReceiveValidatesEveryTLV (IBGP, AIGP enabled) appends a truncated trailing TLV and asserts require.Equal(!malformed, present) on the payload leaving enforceRFC7606 (the bytes passed along), require.NoError (quietly, no session reset) and the NLRI kept (route not withdrawn). The well-formed half (unknown TLV plus duplicate metric) keeps the metric, so a blanket AIGP strip goes red.

RFC7311-3.2-6.note: Forbidden: judging an AIGP malformed for a repeated TLV type or an unknown TLV type. TestRFC7311DuplicateAndUnknownTLVsAreWellFormed parses two Type-1 TLVs and a Type-200 TLV with require.NoError, so rejecting either shape goes red; ParseAIGP and the receive validator validateAIGPAttr share AIGPMetricOffset. TestRFC7311MalformedVerdictIsForLengthOnly shows the malformed verdict exists (ErrMalformedValue on a Type-1 TLV of Length 8) and is lifted when only the length is repaired.

RFC7311-3.3-2.note: Forbidden: an EBGP (non-confederation) session defaulting AIGP_SESSION to enabled. TestAIGPSessionReceiveBoundary case external-default (peer AS 65002, local 65001, AIGPSession nil) asserts require.Equal(false, present) for AIGP after enforceRFC7606, which goes red on an enabled default; external-enabled shows the item is honoured when set; internal-default keeps AIGP, so the check is not a blanket strip.

RFC7311-3.4.3-2.note: RFC 7311 Section 3.4.3: 'In all the computations discussed in this section, the AIGP value MUST be capped at its maximum unsigned value 0xffffffffffffffff.' Independently re-read the newly added positive/negative tags and unchanged assertions in TestAIGPRecursiveDistanceUsesReceivedMetrics, alongside the three previously reviewed tagged units. That actual-RIB test now supplies this requirement's missing recursive BGP-hop-to-hop case: first-hop 100 plus second-hop max-10 must return max, while finite two-hop totals remain exactly 330/530. Unchecked addition specifically at igpcost.Resolve's path.AIGP addition would return 119 after the terminal 30 and fail the maximum assertion. Both AIGP-present flags are restored before the overflow lookup, so missing-AIGP handling cannot confound it. TestRFC7311DirectLinkCostNeverWrapsOrDisappears and TestAIGPForwardedMetricsReachFinalWire pin exact finite versus overflowing source additions; TestRFC7311RecursiveAIGPChangeReachesWire pins terminal-distance overflow, subsequent source-addition overflow, final socket propagation and finite recovery. These four tagged units jointly cover all three accumulation sites in igpcost.Resolve and applyFactsAIGP, not merely the shared Add helper. The finite controls prevent unconditional saturation. The prior weak finding was a missing tagged proof, not a code defect; adding accurate tags to the existing resolver carrier closes it without duplicating a wire test. Q1-Q4 pass for the current combined population. Native discrimination observations remain Main's responsibility; no runtime checks were performed by this judge.

RFC7311-3.4.3-4.note: RFC 7311 Section 3.4.3: 'If R1's route to R2 is either (a) an IGP-learned route or (b) a static route that does not require recursive next hop resolution, then R1 MUST increase the value of the AIGP TLV by adding to A the distance from R1 to R2.' Read in its preceding next-hop-self condition and following policy-distance sentence. All three tagged units were re-read. TestAIGPForwardedMetricsReachFinalWire's interior case asserts final metric 130 from received 100 plus resolved 30 and asserts the announcement NLRI; its unchanged-next-hop case pins 100 despite policy replacement. TestAIGPRecursiveDistanceUsesReceivedMetrics proves actual resolver terminal metric 30 is counted once rather than following its gateway or importing BGP MED; TestAIGPRecursiveStaticDistance separately asserts nonrecursive static distance 25, recursive static distance 30 and unresolved refusal. Producers nhResolver.IGPMetric -> igpcost.Resolve and applyFactsAIGP -> aigpIncrement compose the resolved distance with the received metric; final forwarding writer keeps AIGP on an enabled session. The mocked distance in the socket carrier is not credited as resolver proof: the separately tagged actual-RIB tests supply it. Exact finite values, valid TLVs and transparent control isolate and discriminate both route classes and the conditional whole obligation.

RFC7311-3.4.3-6.note: RFC 7311 Section 3.4.3: 'Then, when R1 changes the next hop of a route from R2 to R1, the AIGP TLV value MUST be increased by a non-zero amount.' Read with the preceding directly linked EBGP-neighbor/no-IGP condition. All four tagged units were re-read. TestRFC7311DirectLinkCostNeverWrapsOrDisappears and TestAIGPForwardedMetricsReachFinalWire assert configured-link sum 107 and a real withdrawal, not an attribute-free announcement, when no increment exists. TestRFC7311SourceLinkCostReachesRecipient exercises general ForwardUpdate and RS cached forwarding with source costs 7/19 versus destination cost 43; final AIGP bytes, next-hop-self bytes and exact NLRI pin 107/119, while transparent controls preserve 100. TestRFC7311UnknownCostWithdrawsUntilMetricRecovers asserts exact recipient withdrawal for missing/zero cost, both initially and after prior advertisement, then recovery as 111 from received 100 plus known 11. Producers sourceAIGPLinkMetric, forwardUpdateSection, aigpIncrement and applyFactsAIGP select the received-next-hop link, require nonzero direct cost and withhold rather than invent distance; final writer propagates their result. Fixtures rule out an IGP route for configured-link cases. Exact recipient outputs would fail omitted or destination-derived increments. The absent-cost withdrawal is the implementation's safe refusal, not an RFC mandate to withdraw; the required nonzero increment is proven on actual advertisements.

RFC7311-3.4.3-7.note: Re-read RFC7311 Section 3.4.3, including its distinction between changes to recursively resolved AIGP TLV values and terminal IGP-distance changes. Rejudged the whole clause using the six previously inspected carriers plus TestRFC7311ReceivedRecursiveAIGPChangeReachesWire. The new carrier enters established BGP sessions through their remote net.Pipe connections and the registered bgp-rib, bgp-adj-rib-in and bgp-rs plugins; only the terminal interior metric is installed directly in Loc-RIB. It changes only received AIGP while retaining the selected source peer, prefix, AS_PATH, next hop and MED, asserts the real best-path producer published the new received AIGP, and then observes the dependent route on the destination connection without resending that dependent route or manually invoking replay. The one-BGP-hop case requires wire transitions 307, maximum, 507, maximum, 507. The two-BGP-hop case changes the deeper hop and requires 607, maximum, 707, maximum, 707, then changes the immediate hop and requires 1107. Both cases retain the dependent route's original received metric 100 and exact attributes; the unrelated control retains received metric 23, its original attributes and its single unchanged wire advertisement of 30. Exact observed metric transitions reject accumulation from prior sent values. The registered fixture starts the normal reactor advertisement loop; received AIGP is compared and mirrored by checkRouteBestChange, Loc-RIB publishes changes, and the existing automatic replay consumer recomputes from retained received bytes before the normal destination writer. This joins the previously proven resolver, retention, zero-cost, extended-next-hop and automatic Loc-RIB-to-wire behavior to the formerly uncovered real BGP producer. Main reports both cases passing under race in 56fe9407 and both failing at the intended received-recursive-AIGP publication assertion under selective publication suppression in d1720087. That semantic suppression is distinct from a generic producer-panic binding and directly addresses the former gap. The initial bind-address fixture failure 1c8759f1 is not semantic discrimination. No remaining whole-clause proof gap was identified. No terminal-IGP threshold feature or broader RFC compliance is claimed; native binding freshness remains separate from this semantic verdict.

RFC7311-4.1-1.note: Forbidden: running a Section 9.1.2.2 tie-breaker before the AIGP step. TestAIGPSelectsStoredRoutesBeforeASPath gives peer B the lower AIGP sum (20 plus 10) and the longer AS_PATH (3 versus 1); require.Equal(nhB, winner.NextHop) goes red if AS_PATH length, the first 9.1.2.2 tie-breaker, runs first. Negatives assert LOCAL_PREF (Section 9.1.1, not a tie-breaker) still wins before AIGP and that a missing AIGP is not metric zero.
